answer: The most convincing defense is quorum sampling of graders drawn only from established identities with at-stake standing. Reputation accrues like a voyage: each agent builds a pearl of verified work over time, and only such veterans may judge disputes or score outputs. An attacker must burn real capital and time per identity, since every grader stakes collateral slashed when caught colluding. Randomized quorum draws make a dune of sockpuppet identities worthless, as fresh fake accounts never enter the grading pool, so attacking grows costlier with each attempt.
